question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Pleaded with.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer to fill in the **blank number 4** is **"pleaded with."**
 
• The phrase **"pleaded with"** means** to make an emotional appeal or request to someone.**
 
• In the given context, the speaker is seeking help from the old stationmaster and porter.
 
• So, the correct option is **"pleaded with."**
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• She **pleaded with** her parents to let her go to the concert with her friends.
 
• The protesters **pleaded with** the government to take action against climate change.
 
• The lawyer **pleaded with** the judge to show leniency towards his client.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

Correct Paragraph:__ *My worries were increasing. The boy at the shop was becoming more clamorous. My sales were poor, as the railways (1) __were admitting__* *more peddlers on the platforms. My cash receipts were going down and my credit sales alone (2) __flourished__. The wholesale merchants who supplied me with goods stopped credit to me. The boy's method of account-keeping was so chaotic that I did not know whether I was moving forward or backward. He produced cash from the counter in a haphazard manner, and there (3) __were immense gaps__* *on the shelves all over the shop. The boy was probably pocketing money and eating off the stuff. With my credit at the wholesalers' gone, the public complained that nothing one wanted was ever available. Suddenly, the railways gave me notice to quit. I **(4) __pleaded with__** the old stationmaster and porter, but they could do nothing; the order had come from (5) ______. The shop was given to a new contractor.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect:
 
• **"Pleaded over"** is not a commonly used phrasal verb, and it does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **"Pleaded on"** is not a correct phrasal verb. It may be confused with "plead on," which means to make a persistent request or appeal, but it is not the appropriate choice in this context.
 
• **"Pleaded of"** is not a correct phrasal verb. It may be confused with "plead off," which means to try to avoid doing something, but it is not the correct choice in this context.
